notes.title: War in Ukraine - despatch 1
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/020e60366ffe1f4d2b56ec7ab691fdfcbcc4cc71.png[/img]

Hello guys!
It has been almost 2 months since we last posted anything here. The reason is that on February 24 Russian Army invaded Ukraine. As some of you may know, our team is located in Kyiv - the capital of Ukraine. Russian troops have been stopped just some 7 km from the city. There has been a number of missile strikes and artillery attacks against the city throughout the last 52 days. 

I will tell you more about how the war started for our team and how we coped with it in the next despatches. For now, I would like to briefly summarize the last two months for you. 

The team was not able to work for around the first 10 days of the war. Then we started to gradually restore our operations. Paying salaries on time was our number one priority that we managed to do - thankfully the banking system of Ukraine works well enough (even though it has certain wartime restrictions that are annoying but both necessary and understandable). 

Since March 7 we are working remotely, even if not at 100% of our usual capacity. We have been gradually restoring our operations to full strength since then. We will have to delay all projects that we are working on but that delay most likely would not be a major one. The key thing is that we keep working and doing our best efforts to finish our projects as soon as possible without diminishing their quality. 

I am sorry for the lack of communication with the community, but we were very busy organizing and maintaining our work in difficult wartime conditions. So, now I finally found some free time to reach out to you guys and update you on the situation. We decided that work is our number one priority and communication will be done when we are capable of running production as planned. Right now things have leveled out to some extent, so we will be communicating with you more often. 

Key thing is that everyone on the team is alive and safe right now (to the extent one can be safe under daily strategic missile strikes). 

I will tell you more in the next despatches. 

With best regards from Kyiv

Oleksandr and the Starni Games team

notes.title: Listen to the Säkkijarven Polkka tack from the Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty
notes.notes:
Hello, guys!

Today, we reveal Säkkijärven polkka - the second historical track from the Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty soundtrack, recorded by Daraba studio. Säkkijärven polkka is a well-known Finnish folk tune that got new life and meaning during the dramatic events of World War II. It got the lyrics sometimes sung with the tune, which stated that while Säkkijärvi itself might have been lost (ceded to the Soviet Union in 1940), the Finns at least still had the polka.

Listen to the "Säkkijärven polkka" track on our YouTube channel: 
[previewyoutube=qa8BnE0QBU4;full][/previewyoutube]

During the Continuation War, the Finnish Army discovered that the retreating Soviets had scattered radio-controlled mines throughout the re-captured city of Viipuri. These mines were set off when a three-note chord was played on the frequency the radio was tuned to. In order to thwart the enemy's goal, Fins started transmitting the Säkkijärvi polka, so that the frequency of the triads used by the enemy was interfered with to the point that the mines were completely unusable.

The Polka surely bolstered the troops' morale during the hardships of the protracted war. 

Thus, this boisterous folk tune became the war-time song and is highly regarded to this day. 

If you want to get access to the whole Strategic Mind series soundtrack with all the high-quality recordings - feel free to check out our Franchise soundtrack on Steam:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1358280/Strategic_Mind_Franchise_Soundtrack/
Have a good day!
Starni Games team

Hello!

Christmas holidays are in full swing and it is high time to look back and summarize everything we have done throughout 2021.

[h3][url=https://mailchi.mp/starnigames.com/christmas-wallpapers]👉 Subscribe to Starni Games newsletter and get the special wallpapers[/url][/h3]

[h1]3 March | Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty announcement[/h1]

Early into the year, we finalized our plans for the next game in the Strategic Mind series - we did niche games before, but now we dared to start working on a niche game with a niche setting. We really hope that you guys will like the project and support it. 

https://steamcommunity.com/games/1381850/announcements/detail/3059604354539711195

In April we have finally set the exact release date for Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom and shared a Story trailer for the upcoming release. 

[previewyoutube=ol8CWwA2qvI;full][/previewyoutube]

In may we have successfully released the Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom. You can check out the game and its Cinematic trailer following the link below:

https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1381850/view/3059611965013023855
Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom is the newest and definitely most well-polished game across the series. We can only hope and work very hard to make sure that the Spirit of Liberty would be able to set the bar even higher.

notes.title: Listen to the Finlandia Op. 26 tack from the Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty
notes.notes:
Hello, guys!

Today we reveal the first historical track from the Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty, recorded by Daraba studio. Finlandia Op. 26 is by far the longest and most epic of all the tracks we asked Daraba studio to create for the Strategic Mind series so far. I guess every Fin would know it, but for the rest of the audience here are a few facts from the historical perspective:

"Finlandia, Op. 26, is a tone poem by the Finnish composer Jean Sibelius. The piece was composed for the Press Celebrations of 1899, a covert protest against increasing censorship from the Russian Empire.
In order to avoid Russian censorship, Finlandia had to be performed under alternative names at various musical concerts. Titles under which the piece masqueraded were numerous and often confusing —famous examples include "Happy Feelings at the awakening of Finnish Spring", and "A Scandinavian Choral March"."

Listen to the "Finlandia Op. 26" track on our YouTube channel: 

[previewyoutube=MkRnCFZdMs8;full][/previewyoutube]
We want to thank everyone, who purchased Strategic Mind Franchise Soundtrack - your support really helped us get more historical tracks added into the game. We are also very grateful to everyone who participated in the community votes and helped us choose the best tracks. Here is the result of the combined efforts of the community and our team. All Spirit of Liberty tracks will be added to the Strategic Mind Franchise Soundtrack at the game's release. 

If you want to get access to the whole Strategic Mind series soundtrack with all the high-quality recordings - feel free to check out our Franchise soundtrack on Steam:

notes.title: Games Gathering Kyiv 2021 Conference
notes.notes:
Hello, guys!

On December 4-5th our team went to one of the biggest annual Games Conferences in Eastern Europe, which was conveniently held in our hometown - Kyiv. We bought tickets for all team members who wanted to come - that means everyone really. Fortunately, we also got a few tickets for free as speakers and Indie Blast participants.  

It was a truly massive event for Game industry specialists with some 2800 people attending offline and extra 600 online. It was a great opportunity to talk to colleagues, discuss all the latest news, share experiences and just chill with like-minded people. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/e6daaea3e40a93abee163a18755edb272c68c374.jpg[/img]
Large conference hall

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/eb6268f0867942038b7f315abd90825210ac982c.jpg[/img]
Wargaming brought the real T-34-85 tank to their booth and made a lottery winning which granted a free ride in the T-34-85 tank. Quite thematic I would say. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/fd9b537b0fa32e940734d3e3c2209c848fef286c.jpg[/img]
The insides of the T-34-58 tank. Although refitted with these fancy modern LEDs to increase combat capabilities, this new equipment provides +99 style and -50 spotting. 

[h1]Indie Blast[/h1]
Now, closer to our team’s involvement in the event. It is our good tradition to present our Strategic Mind titles in the Indie Blast competition that allows us to have a small booth sponsored by Epic Games for developers working on Unreal Engine 4. So, this time was no different and we presented our upcoming title - Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/231aade8f29ade12633b933a0d0beacf66fe83ae.jpg[/img]
Starni Games booth at the event

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/cfce3cb65fbfc2ec98fe2638e5f50b8b52d501f7.jpg[/img]
Starni team - everyone hides from the camera (they seem to have a very high camouflage parameter and are shown as "?")

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/ffa90a7205be799872da2bf4effbdc107b25708e.jpg[/img]
Visitors trying out the game. They obviously failed - one cannot just play our game at a conference successfully. It requires some more time to really get into it. :)

[h1]Starni team at Games Gathering[/h1]
This time we set a record of all 14-people-team attendance. Here are some photos that were taken by our team during the event:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/fcf31c2e96c20ef6e7412fcc8b0fb686ffff6c35.jpg[/img]
Kate Bovkun - the one and only 2D artist in our team :) Now she has finally found herself a teammate ;)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/7f36552429132bcb825623f436e9c204fc58129a.jpg[/img]
Alex Marchenko - our Lead Level Designer, ... at least that is what it says on the badge. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/0070da4fdd3fa9096bd1dd46f71f2c347cb93d7a.jpg[/img]
Valentine Kolesnikov - our Level Design Guru (also known for the best memes), even the famous David Mullich himself has asked to take a photo with Valentine. ;) (not really)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/3195cf424383255ae022c32f0b2907ad504523db.jpg[/img]
Kate Bovkun and Alexander Shevchuk are enjoying themselves at the luxurious booth of some big gaming company that makes Hidden Object games. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/5e5bbf8b3ee2ab082a865b25c75c30271d3fd076.jpg[/img]
Valentine Kolesnikov and Alex Marchenko taking some photos together to strengthen team spirit. No, just kidding - they made those photos to get free lollipops.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/23530f18d9a48fbd0abfb0130f5b0d51be6338ae.jpg[/img]
Our marketing and community manager Katya Globa is taking photos with her sister, oops it's not her sister, it is Lerika Mallayeva the CEO & Founder of DevGAMM events (big game dev conferences similar to this one).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/87205c4df40465c252809cce0d646b7699d65dcd.jpg[/img]
Aaaand finally, Alex Marchenko is taking photos with his new buddy David Mullich and talking about the development of Heroes of Might and Magic VIII. (not really)

[h1]Publisher vs Developer talk[/h1]
Our CEO Ihor Tymoshenko and COO Oleksandr Sienin had a 1-hour talk about Developer-Publisher relations: how to look for the right publisher, what things to have in mind during the negotiations, and other such things. The key takeaway would be that you have to look for a very specific publisher that fits your company and project the best and the one you can build a long-term relationship with mutual trust and respect. You should be partners, not “the boss and the subordinate”.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/807cc8cd44bac33139c4deae68a615a01b205029.jpg[/img]
Left to right: Ihor Tymoshenko and Oleksandr Sienin just started with the talk. Must be really hard to give a talk with your mouth closed. ;)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/6a7170600ad8dacc2765fd99eadf149385b5a455.jpg[/img]
The talk has not progressed much since the photo above, as could be seen from the slides. 

[h1]An unexpected guest[/h1]
One of the most famous guests of the conference was undoubtedly David Mullich - the Producer of the Heroes of Might and Magic series (HoMM 3 and HoMM 4), Vampires the Masquerade Bloodlines, and many other famous titles. It was a pleasant surprise when David came to our small booth as he was visiting the Indie zone. We told him about the Strategic Mind series, and he said that really liked how the cinematic trailer for the Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom was directed (footage cut and overall visuals) - it was shown on the screen at our booth as we spoke. We could not miss the chance and took a couple of photos with David. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/864a0dc02864d862e81c0091a9eaf10b4c4e0449.jpg[/img]
David Mullich and Oleksandr Sienin at Starni Games booth. Yay!

The next day David Mullich taught a lecture about the development of the HoMM series and his path in game development. It was very interesting since the guys on the team could really sympathize and reflect on many things he spoke about - since we often face the same problems.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/9324d646bdb63771659cbbe214080a20c7e87082.jpg[/img]
One of the slides from the David Mullich talk at the event explains the UI visual style that the HoMM3 dev team has very fittingly dubbed "the fecal brush". Did not stop them from creating an immortal game though. :)

[h1]Our new project[/h1]
Interesting thing was that since the conference was before the 14th December - when Slitherine had officially announced our new joint project Headquarters: World War II - we could not really talk about it, and kept talking about “some unannounced project". Fortunately, now the announcement has come and we finally can talk about it more or less freely. We invite you to check out the store page for and wishlist + follow to keep an eye on the development. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1840800/Headquarters_World_War_II/

Have a good day!
Starni Games team

notes.title: Headquarters: World War II - Our New Project in Partnership With Slitherine
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/600a47f6590584ad58f8a4e14a5761d8ba9082d2.png[/img]

Hello guys!

The year is about to end, but we have one more big surprise in store for you.

Yesterday, our new project - Headquarters: World War II - was announced by Slitherine during the Home of Wargamers live stream:

[previewyoutube=WIaGkFdM6n0;full][/previewyoutube]
Headquarters: World War II is our first project with a publisher, and not just any publisher, but the number one publisher for niche strategy games - Slitherine. We are very happy with how the cooperation is going so far and we think that this project has everything it needs to become a very interesting and fun game for you guys to play. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/4c26df2c1721ff6d41714c95b1c8d596d70b01e9.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/7c281591534455c9257d0f90a70e93a71a8ec092.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/1d7ae3c107121eee35a49dfb0894c433535be280.jpg[/img]

Headquarters: World War II is a tactical level game on a smaller scale compared to the Strategic Mind series. That allowed us to use real objects’ scale and bring the graphics to the new level of realism as well as deepen the combat tactics by taking into account attack angle and tank’s front/side/back/top armor planting, and adding different levels of terrain elevation. It features the Battle of Normandy in three plot-driven campaigns from the UK, US and German perspectives, as well as skirmish mode and multiplayer.

notes.title: Gameplay Trailer for the Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty is Out!
notes.notes:
Hello guys!

We are happy to reveal the first trailer for the upcoming Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty. It shows mostly key game mechanics and units - so there will probably be few surprises for the seasoned veterans of the Strategic Mind series, but we hope that it will bring in more new players.

[previewyoutube=1-hj1I5Gh-Q;full](trailer link)[/previewyoutube]
There is also a fly in the ointment - we have to move the Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty release to a later date. We can say for sure that it will be released in 2022, and right now we aim for the Q3 release, with a free Prologue release a few months before the full title. There are various reasons for the delay, one of them is an increased studio workload. On the bright side, we aim to get the game as ready as possible before the release instead of rushing it.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1683420/Strategic_Mind_Spirit_of_Liberty__Prologue_1939/
We are also hiring new people to the team to speed up the process. We have got 2 new team members in September: Vova is our new Programmer and Dmitriy is our new 3D Artist. So, we grew to 15 people in the office. We are looking for a couple more people to join the team later this year. 

We will provide a detailed report on the current state of the project in our newsletter. So, if you want to know what exactly is ready at this stage and what is lagging behind - you can subscribe to Starni Games newsletter and get all the inside news.

notes.title: Survey 2.0 Results
notes.notes:
Hello guys!

Last week we ran a community survey 2.0 about the importance of the various elements of the game. We got 49 responses [url=https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf1O5PxiMyFmQUvg_4pKR93fcFc8VpiGMEECpAZDAv0UslLcw/viewform?usp=sf_link]via google form[/url] and 23 across our Community hubs on Steam. 

We want to say thank you to all participants for your effort and for sharing your thoughts and ideas with us - we have studied your feedback and found lots of valuable insights there. Some of your ideas we will keep in mind while making the first gameplay trailer for the Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty as key points for it. While other insights will help us develop the game in the direction that will be more meaningful and valuable for most players. 

Here are the results of survey 2.0. But before that, a small recap about the survey's rules: Below you can find the list of key aspects of the game in our view. These aspects are given in a randomized order to avoid bias. Rate their importance for you personally on a scale of 5, where 5 is very important and 0 is not important at all. Please notice, that different key aspects can get the same number of points.

[h1]Results of survey 2.0[/h1]

1. All unit models are historical and become available at historically accurate time of the campaign. Same with the enemy troops. | Example: Historically Finland had very limited military equipment and was purchasing it from different countries, so you will get to create your own mishmash of historically available units: Command the Finnish Infantry and Bofors AT guns, Swedish Recon cars, captured Soviet vehicles, including BT-7, T-34, and KV tanks. Make use of pre-war British Bristol Blenheim bombers, covered by Dutch Fokker and US Buffalo fighter planes. Purchase German Pz-IV tanks, StuG assault guns, and Ju-88 bombers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/130fe5bd450f49cab7a18fe8a8f6661ea2a54a3d.png[/img]

2. Between the battles you can learn Headquarters skills that allow you to get unique tactical advantages. Command points system allows the flexible balance of the number of deployed troops - the more you deploy the less active HQ skills you can use. | Example: Your artillery could fire twice per turn, or your Aircraft units could land and take off without losing movement points.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/8264b312cdbb0c2b357f18b188d1aaa171bea49e.png[/img]

3. Lots of unit classes: Infantry, Tanks, Artillery, Anti-tank guns, Anti-aircraft guns, Assault guns, Armoured trains, Reconnaissance cars, Fighters, Tactical bombers, Strategic bombers, Submarines, Destroyers, Heavy cruisers, Battleships, and Carriers. All units have their unique skills and set of level-up abilities and equipment. | Example: you can even use Armored trains (including the legendary Saviour of Karelia) or Railroad artillery installations that are rare guests in digital wargames.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/bcac724e7f38c25b46f9fc38e0a08492111a8775.png[/img]

4. (hi)story-driven gameplay. | Example: lots of primary and secondary objectives with in-game dialogue by historical figures. Completing certain objectives provides unique global bonuses or trophies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/f3cfea65844ba61f403fdfcbb305e0b7b20911a0.png[/img]

5. Classical wargame with modern 3D graphics created with Unreal Engine 4. | Example: you can see close up shots of tanks and other units moving with real physics across uneven terrain and enjoy the realistic 3D unit models instead of the usual counters.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/061b8d4aa12436cb562701a43b64aa8e98cd4ab1.png[/img]

6. You can gain Heroes throughout the campaign and assign them to chosen units. All heroes are historical figures and allow units to get special powerful skills. | Example: The deadliest sniper in WW2 history - Simo Häyhä - will join your troopsWith 542 confirmed kills, and an unconfirmed total number of 705, not only was Simo Häyhä the deadliest sniper of World War II, but perhaps the deadliest sniper of all time. His nickname “the White Death” was well-earned.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/aed95b892e8d94848eecdea2f0c5adc54cb40769.png[/img]

7. Different victory types, awards and ranks. You get different victory types based on your performance throughout the operations. That determines what awards you get and when you will be promoted to the next rank. | Example: All awards and ranks are not just an insignia, but provide gameplay bonuses - higher ranks means more Command points, while awards also provide discounts for units and make the HQ unit stronger.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/8aaef641d6efe6a5e2cce9383412d62bdf220310.png[/img]

8. Cinematics - around 70 minutes in each title. | Example: before and after every operation you watch a cinematics sequence with historical characters delving deeper into the events of WW2 and the historical flow.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/28ca846a2c654472a8bf9c66e624ad6440035e68.png[/img]

9. Advanced supply system - great depth with little micromanagement. | Example: There are different types of Infrastructure across the map. Supply points transport the supplies across the map. If you break the supply chain by damaging, capturing or cutting off (blocking with ZoC) its elements - the enemy troops will be left without supplies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/6875ce9ba8b6187305a3b1acc27ae0dd9b0eec19.png[/img]

10. Both historical (75%) and alternate history (25%) operations. | Example: You can enjoy both real historical battles and explore “what if” outcomes based on real plans and were never realised, like Sea Lion, or Operation Unthinkable.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/968b13a2493988997cee8ccfa54048f258ea298f.png[/img]

11. Improved combat system - lethal vs nonlethal damage, 4 levels of spotting, various skills and equipment, significance of terrain, LoS and ZoC, different weather conditions and nighttime. | Example: the tactical moves feel quite diverse thanks to the original Panzer General mechanics that went through a very significant rework and upgrade.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/381dce367ed7a9735473fb3f9e33a30d1253e109.png[/img]

12. Advanced transportation system - ground transport (trucks and APCs), train, aircraft or ship transportation. | Example: all ground units can be assigned truck or APC they board if they have to move far - at the same time they are vulnerable while in transit. Additionally, you can board trains, ships and aircraft for large distance troops transfer and landing operations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/a4d145507a4261fbbe929bb852f04373683fae65.png[/img]

13. All types of units can get special equipment, allowing you to finetune your troops to better tackle the task at hand. | Example: Units can get diverse equipment such as: flamethowers, sappers squad, mortars, recoilless rifles, smoke generators, torpedoes, incendiary shells, or even dummy tanks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/41807bb80b05c92f94050d649f2dde2989666bb8.png[/img]

14. Upgrade units to newer models to carry over crew’s experience. Out of line upgrades are more expensive. | Example: Upgrading Pz IV C to Pz IV F is much cheaper than replacing it with a Tiger II.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/51802a38de7098ff90bbe4a2c99a554f3afb3866.png[/img]

15. Advanced naval combat system - all ships have parts such as all sorts of armament, hull, engine, flight deck, etc. with their own HP and functionality that deteriorates as they are getting damaged. | Example: Ship has extra defense when its Engine part is operational. When the engine is damaged the ship loses its movement points and the extra defense it had due to mobility. Same with all types of guns etc. The maintenance team repairs the ship overtime, but you could also use the emergency repair team in case your ship is in dire straits.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/f5ecd02612fb0da06967dea5063fc3f2624dae66.png[/img]

16. You can play some of the enemy units as well, if you manage to capture them during the battles. | Example: In Spirit of Liberty Finns can get their hands on Russian BT--7s, T-34s, KV-1s, ISU-152 and other cool stuff.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/f8a5ed734b347573600b5a24b822d013cdb2e244.png[/img]

17. All units gain experience and can learn additional skills every time they level up. | Example: Infantry can get a Forced march level up skill allowing it to move 2 extra Move points 3 times per operation. Artillery can learn to move 1 tile after firing to quickly change its position etc.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/b5073519ef2ba10c23ac2c63f910e33af9ddeb58.png[/img]

Make sure to wishlist Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty - Prologue 1939 to get notification when the free prologue goes live. As always we do appreciate all sorts of useful feedback from the players - so make sure to share your thoughts with us after playing the Prologue.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1683420/Strategic_Mind_Spirit_of_Liberty__Prologue_1939/

notes.title: Community Survey: What is Your Favourite Element of Strategic Mind Games?
notes.notes:
As developers we cannot help but feel attached to virtually all aspects of our games. Yet we are curious which of them are the most relevant for the players. So, we decided to ask the community what are the most important elements of the game for you. Please, help us out by sharing your thoughts on the subject - that would be a great help.

Below you can find the list of key aspects of the game in our view. They are presented in a randomly generated order to avoid bias. Please choose up to 8 key elements and put them by the order of significance:
1 = [b]8 points[/b] = most significant
2 = [b]7 points[/b] = very significant
...
8 = [b]1 point[/b] = less significant
9-17 = [b]0 points[/b] = not very significant.
Please, explain your reasoning if you can. You can also add your own points under the list in case we have missed anything. 

We hope that your answers will help us promote the series more effectively and increase the players community. That in turn will help ensure longevity and further improvement of the series, so your support is very important for us. 

[h3]Example of how your answer could be structured:[/h3]
1. 10) Both historical (75%) and alternate history (25%) operations.
Because I love history but without alternate scenarios it is a bit dull.
2. 15) Advanced naval combat system.
Since I enjoy naval combat, this system is really different from any other game.
3. 3) Lots of unit classes.
I enjoy combined arms operations and the tactical flexibility/diversity it allows.
4. 7) Different victory types, awards and ranks.
I dislike games that do not give me a sense of achievement. I also like that the achievements are meaningful in the Strategic Mind. 
5. 4) (hi)story-driven gameplay.
I like that I also learn something new about history while playing, and often it is really interesting. 
6. 17) All units gain experience and can learn additional skills every time they level up.
I like that my army is getting more powerful and experienced as the campaign progresses.
7. 9) Advanced supply system - great depth with little micromanagement.
I think it is something many games miss - a proper supply system.
8. 13) All types of units can get special equipment.
Once again the more customization and control I have over my units - the better.

All units have their unique skills and set of level-up abilities and equipment. 
[b]Example:[/b] You can even use Armored trains (including the legendary Saviour of Karelia) or Railroad artillery installations that are rare guests in digital wargames. 

[b]4)[/b] (hi)story-driven gameplay
[b]Example:[/b] Lots of primary and secondary objectives with in-game dialogue by historical figures. Completing certain objectives provides unique global bonuses or trophies.

[b]5)[/b] Classical wargame with modern 3D graphics created with Unreal Engine 4.

[b]6)[/b] You can gain Heroes throughout the campaign and assign them to chosen units. All heroes are historical figures and allow units to get special powerful skills.
[b]Example:[/b] The deadliest sniper in WW2 history - Simo Häyhä - will join your troops
With 542 confirmed kills, and an unconfirmed total number of 705, not only was Simo Häyhä the deadliest sniper of World War II, but perhaps the deadliest sniper of all time. His nickname “the White Death” was well-earned.

[b]8)[/b] Cinematics - around 70 minutes in each title 
[b]Example:[/b] Before and after every operation you watch a cinematics sequence with historical characters delving deeper into the events of WW2 and the historical flow.

[b]9)[/b] Advanced supply system - great depth with little micromanagement
[b]Example:[/b] There are different types of Infrastructure across the map. Supply points transport the supplies across the map. If you break the supply chain by damaging, capturing or cutting off (blocking with ZoC) its elements - the enemy troops will be left without supplies.

[b]10)[/b] Both historical (75%) and alternate history (25%) operations.
[b]Example:[/b] You can enjoy both real historical battles and explore “what if” outcomes based on real plans and were never realised, like Sea Lion, or Operation Unthinkable. 

[b]11)[/b] Improved combat system - lethal vs nonlethal damage, 4 levels of spotting, various skills and equipment, significance of terrain, LoS and ZoC, different weather conditions and nighttime. 
[b]Example:[/b] The tactical moves feel quite diverse thanks to the original Panzer General mechanics that went through a very significant rework and upgrade. 

[b]12)[/b] Advanced transportation system - ground transport (trucks and APCs), train, aircraft or ship transportation. 
[b]Example:[/b] All ground units can be assigned truck or APC they board if they have to move far - at the same time they are vulnerable while in transit. Additionally, you can board trains, ships and aircraft for large distance troops transfer and landing operations. 

[b]13)[/b] All types of units can get special equipment, allowing you to finetune your troops to better tackle the task at hand.
[b]Example:[/b] Units can get diverse equipment such as: flamethowers, sappers squad, mortars, recoilless rifles, smoke generators, torpedoes, incendiary shells, or even dummy tanks.  

[b]14)[/b] Upgrade units to newer models to carry over crew’s experience. Out of line upgrades are more expensive. 
[b]Example:[/b] Upgrading Pz IV C to Pz IV F is much cheaper than replacing it with a Tiger II.

[b]15)[/b] Advanced naval combat system - all ships have parts such as all sorts of armament, hull, engine, flight deck, etc. with their own HP and functionality that deteriorates as they are getting damaged.
[b]Example:[/b] Ship has extra defense when its Engine part is operational. When the engine is damaged the ship loses its movement points and the extra defense it had due to mobility. Same with all types of guns etc. The maintenance team repairs the ship overtime, but you could also use the emergency repair team in case your ship is in dire straits.

[b]16)[/b] You can play some of the enemy units as well, if you manage to capture them during the battles.
[b]Example:[/b] In Spirit of Liberty Finns can get their hands on Russian BT--7s, T-34s, KV-1s, ISU-152 and other cool stuff.

[b]17)[/b] All units gain experience and can learn additional skills every time they level up.
[b]Example:[/b] Infantry can get a Forced march level up skill allowing it to move 2 extra Move points 3 times per operation. Artillery can learn to move 1 tile after firing to quickly change its position etc. 

Looking forward to discussing the community survey results with you
Starni Games team

notes.title: We Need Your Help! [RESULTS]
notes.notes:
Hello, guys! 

Last week we asked for your thoughts about the best fitting Store page screenshots types for the upcoming game Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty. We were pleasantly surprised by the amount of feedback we got. You have provided a detailed analysis of existing screenshots for previous Strategic Mind titles' and useful ideas for future screenshots. As developers, sometimes it is hard for us to see the game through the players' eyes, so your feedback is invaluable for us. Now we want to believe that we understand you a little bit better. So we appreciate all of your efforts, guys! We will try to heed your advice when working on the Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty screenshots revamp soon, as we now have more materials for them. 

We want to share with you some quotes from the community on Steam and on Reddit about the Strategic Mind screenshots. Maybe it would be interesting for you to read and compare your ideas with the other players' perceptions, or even find your own commentary here:

[h3]1. Zoomed-out strategic view type of screenshot:[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/4afbfcbe5dbe4ca5ae39ab6f4327c9c365b103e7.png[/img]
[b]Likes:[/b] 5
[b]Quotes: [/b]
-I like #1 - it shows a strategic view or something like that? I like to know what kind of tools a strategic game offers.
- The first one should be a little less zoomed out
- Looks like a different game.
- Don’t highlight interesting parts of the game.
- #1 is lovely. it shows you can have different combat arms of the army (air, navy, land/marine), and shows you can have more than just tiny snippet of forces.

[h3]2. HQ room type of screenshot:[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/068f7c1e29a57087167d8981eea73fa90f80f81c.png[/img]
[b]Likes[/b]: 9
[b]Quotes:[/b]
- #2 is something I would not appreciate on a strategy game page. That's a neat visual for a menu but that's not what I'm going to actually play, so it's kind of just noise.
- I'd avoid anything like 2. that sort of stuff could just be done with photo likeness written dialogue like other games have handled it.

I know it seems like some sort of special feature of these games but for me personally it is a put off a bit as I'm more interested in the challenge of the scenarios or the campaign than wading through some sort of' 'marionette' cut scene where a simple military style 'old school' dossier of the assignment or objective would be more immersive if done authentically maybe with a voice over like some game leaders in this field have done in the past because it's efficient for the player and adds enough immersion to get to the 'real' game
- Some people are looking for fast-casual playing similar to multiplayer game but many other people when play a single player campaign don't want just a chain of battles with a poor and forgetable introduction between them. They look for a full story and want to "make the difference" with their choices and actions. On the other hand, most games just show an "intro video" and a final "victory video". I love the work you made to create a screenplay and a background to connect every battle and the consecuences of the previous clashes like the image of Picture Number 2 and the mini-videos between battles. Screenshots should reflect that your game is more than a chain of battles with an "excuse-plot".
-  Looks interesting, Using that would be good.
- I love this shot. Shows that there is more to the game than just standard RTS fare and clicking/moving units.
- Great, but maybe highlight the campaign map though instead of a general. 
- I think this kind of image should always be included to the screenshots. Player spends a lot of time in this room, so it should at-least be represented (also it would remind the player that it's mostly story-driven).

[h3]3. Battlefield view with No UI and No hexes type of screenshot:[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/72365c7b5d570b6b89888c0cef0885081337262d.png[/img]
[b]Likes:[/b] 7
[b]Quotes:[/b]
-  I always appreciate when a strategy can boast atmospheric screenshots like #3 and #7. As much as strategic games are about maps and figures, many people still prefer games that let you feel "in the moment" rather than being purely schematic.
- Beautiful.
- Looks like an animated sequence? This one is confusing. Because there is no grid.
- This shot looks very Indie. Some people like that, some people don't.
- Not a fan sadly. It looks without UI like it's just a image where we arrive into, when departing from a cut-scene.

[h3]4. Equipment UI type of screenshot:[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/f173556268d2e5c1c80274a5bac1040fafbd2fe4.png[/img]
[b]Likes:[/b] 9
[b]Quotes: [/b]
- This is really good and helpful picture! It shows you have plenty of options to customize your units (and their secondary roles due to it).
- I think #4 is a great UI screenshot - it's not too simplistic like basic overlay, and it looks like it's well-readable.
- I like your efforts to customize units with skill upgrades, special equipment addition, etc. as it can be seen in Picture Number 4.
- I can't read or undestand that info so I wouldn't use that one.
- Obligatory "under the hood" shot, but a good one, I think. Gotta let people know that there is depth to be found here and this pic does it.

[h3]5. Battlefield view with UI and without hexes type of screenshot:[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/fac45106b5dc28191b02aa3c8966956194a68099.png[/img]
[b]Likes:[/b] 15
[b]Quotes:[/b] 
- From my point of view 7 and 5, this gives me more information about features of the game, such as the grid system, the types of buildings in the game, as well as these are the most atmospheric pictures for my taste
- I liked 5 the most. Not too less, and bot too much information clustered at one spot.
- Seems to be another good shot of the game.
- Show me exactly what kind of game this is.
- This pic covers what you'll be seeing most of the time, I believe, and that's important. A great "first-impression" shot. I would lead with this one.
- Might suggest injecting the mouse cursor, showing some highlighted units or something, show me a little more of how the game works. 

[b]6. Close up units view type of screenshot:[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/1dbf0d57e06f853f1fc9f34759d7e70bfb83dd22.png[/img]
[b]Likes:[/b] 8
[b]Quotes:[/b] 
- I'd probably go for looking up close and detailed like in 6.
- I wouldn't use that, doesn't seem like the game you will be playing.
- Pretty but not something I care about. Some others would though!
- In your provided examples the 2 and 6 ones really call out to me.
- Graphic quality is not the most important for hardcore and veteran players (if we have played with prehistoric 3D graphics of "Alone in the dark" or "Colonization" pixels we can play everything) but for casual players and young people it could be a decisive factor so you should include some screenshots like Picture Number 6 showing units closely with zoom to satisfy these people expectations about graphics.

[h3]7. Battlefield view with No UI and with hexes type of screenshot:[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/917afa333da48c6c00b4813549244e7db57cf8e5.png[/img]
[b]Likes:[/b] 19
[b]Quotes:[/b]
- Me personally I like screenshot 7 the most:
1) it shows (at least that's what I assume) where your game camera is mostly focused;
2) It looks pretty polished and clean (not to much the viewer can focus on);
3) Would be a good image to place a logo on top or something.
- Image 7 makes the game look best imo.
- I think this is my favorite. Another grand-scale pic showing the expanse of the map, along with the grids on the ground showing me a little bit of how the game works and a tiny piece of what to expect. This one makes me want to try the game.
- This should be your lead off shot IMO.
- 7.
- 7 looks the most attractive for me.
- I like the 5th one and the 7th.
- Is really nice screen shot, even for one without an UI. It's atmospheric. It shows more nations than one (telling that there's a chance to fight more than just Germans/Soviets!) And in general looks good, but it probably better to let fans take these ones than to have at a store front?

[h3]8. Battlefield view with UI and without hexes type of screenshot[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/b7de301b23386460d8c3e2feb45dabaa6302f262.png[/img]
[b]Likes: [/b]10
[b]Quotes:[/b] 
-  Looks like how you'll be playing most of the game?
- This one shows exactly what type of game it is with a little extra complexity.
- This image is way too early taken. Everything is in their static starting positions and it looks more like a chess game than how the game plays. Please let at-least one turn be done before screen-shots as it looks more like a staring match than an active battlefield.

Please, let us know what you think about this whole discussion. Do you agree with the fellow players?
Is there any screenshot type that is really needed but is missing from our selection? Looking forward to further discussion.

Starni Games team

notes.title: The Day World War II Ended
notes.notes:
September 2 marks the signing of the Japanese Instrument of Surrender, which officially put an end to World War II. Starting on 1 September 1939, the war lasted for 6 years and 1 day, and took the lives of 75-80 million people, more than half of them - civilians. It left a mark on the world that persists even today, after the cities have all been rebuilt, some from ground up.

For most, World War II is staunchly associated with the fighting in Europe: the endless marching columns of the Wehrmacht soldiers, the bombed out moonscapes of the European cities, and the massive Soviet tank charges sweeping across the Russian steppes. It is all too easy to forget that this terrible war did not, in fact, end on May 8 - there were 4 months of bitter fighting left to be done after the Victory in Europe.

For Germany, the war was over, but for many Germans it was not. Minefields had to be cleared, repairs made, and crimes - punished. The long and arduous process of Denazification and reintegration had begun.

The Soviet Union had its hands full as well, with rebuilding its own territories and policing the occupied ones. In August, when it became clear the Japanese wouldn’t surrender without a fight, the USSR gave it to them, invading Manchuria and crushing the Kwantung Army.

For many American servicemen, the Victory in Europe was distant and ephemeral. Tens of thousands would die on the atolls of the Pacific until the US would deploy the final drastic measure - the nearly mythical Atomic Bomb.

As the last member of the Axis standing, the Empire of Japan held out until August, but now, its resolve was completely broken.

All the while, the small but brave nation of Finland, still formally at war with both the Soviet Union and the United Kingdom, was starting to rebuild. Its war against the Soviet Union, and the brief struggle against the Nazi Germany left swaths of the countryside destroyed by “scorched earth” tactics. There would be plenty of trials - show trials, most of them. But in the end, Finland had the distinction of being the only Soviet neighbour that fought most of the war as a German ally, but survived as a free democracy. It was a hard-won peace that still reigns today.

You will have a chance to see how it all started for Finland in our upcoming free Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty Prologue 1939 app featuring the first month of the Winter War. Make sure you do not miss it by Wishlisting and Following the project:

notes.title: Units In Spirit of Liberty #1
notes.notes:
At the outbreak of the Winter War, Finland’s tank forces were all but nonexistent. To be precise, on paper they had around thirty-two obsolete Renault FT tanks, some Vickers-Carden-Lloyd Mk. IVs and Model 33s, which were equipped with machine guns, and 26 Vickers Armstrongs 6-ton tanks. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/f9e98bf337cf66a0950bcc344c9e7fa7d76850ec.png[/img]

The Finns even had to rearm the British Vickers 6-tons with a Finnish made (licensed production in Finland) 37 mm Bofors AT-guns. Only 13 of these tanks managed to get to the front in time to participate in the battles. Vickers 6-ton tanks were also licenced to the USSR becoming T-26 Soviet tanks, and were the basis for the Polish 7TP tanks.   

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39987147/9e00c62b2eef9551c822547c51c792d71d3fd7d6.jpg[/img]

On 26 February 1940, the Finns employed their Vickers 6-ton tanks for the first – and only – time against Soviet armour. Out of thirteen Finnish Vickers 6-ton tanks available only six were in fighting condition and able to participate in the first assault on the Soviet lines – to make matters worse, one of the tanks was forced to stop, unable to cross a wide trench. The remaining five continued onwards a few hundred meters but ran into dozens of Soviet tanks in the village of Honkaniemi. The Finnish tanks managed to knock out three Soviet tanks but were soon themselves knocked-out.

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/5yKOz1iGjbGvIIrkhQ/giphy.gif?cid=790b7611eb65f46cafd33a3b056321b7408b62df92787ced&rid=giphy.gif&ct=g[/img]

This story clearly shows that tank battles were clearly not the Finnish army’s forte. If we look at the number of tanks both sides had in the Winter War the difference is unbelievably stark:

[list][*] Finland - [b]32 tanks[/b] 
[*] Soviet Union - [b]6 541 tanks[/b][/list]
It is truly a miracle (and a bit of rough terrain, ill suited for tank battles) that the Finnish troops managed to hold out against such odds. Only the heroic struggle of the Finnish Infantry troops made it possible. 

[h2]In the game[/h2]

In the Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty we will have other tanks under the Finnish flag, mostly captured Soviet tanks and some German-supplied Pz IV ones.

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/z2FbpgjvEjsiQiONZA/giphy.gif?cid=790b7611001a01543e0cc1ef7c37afa2d157292d226e1673&rid=giphy.gif&ct=g[/img]

Stay tuned for more updates on the Finnish units in the upcoming Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty and wishlist our free app Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty Prologue 1939 to be the first one to try out the mighty Vickers tanks.

notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40855916/7274719b352d91e380e65363f1d7a17fa94bfffc.png[/img]

Hello, guys! Some of you probably remember the community vote we held when deciding the historical tracks lineup for the Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom. We think it worked out greatly, so now we are back with the new vote regarding the Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty.

We want to let you participate in the Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty development and help us choose the best tracks that will then be recreated by our partners - Daraba Studio to serve as the game soundtrack.


[h2]Our goals:[/h2]
[list][*] We want to select 5 tracks that for sure will be in Spirit of Liberty.
[*] We will most likely pick at least one track from each of the Classics, Marches, and Propaganda categories below. 
[*] [b]Note![/b] All tracks we create will be instrumental (no voice). So, while we link some songs for the reference, there will be only tunes in game. Make sure to take that into account when you make your choice. Some tracks might lose much of their value without the voice.
[*] All tracks we link are just the reference and the final tracks we create for the game might differ significantly in the way they are performed and their length.[/list]
[h2]Rules:[/h2]
[list][*] Choose one of our community hubs and post your choices there - multiple entries by a single Steam account do not stack. 
[*] Choose 5 tracks you like most and rank them. The number one gets 5 points, number two gets 4 points, etc. Example vote:
1. Jean Sibelius - Karelia - Intermezzo [gets 5 points]
2. Vapaussoturin Valloituslaulu [gets 4 points]
3. Njet, Molotoff! [gets 3 points]
4. Jääkärimarssi [gets 2 points]
5. Säkkijärven polkka [gets 1 point]
[*] The more points the track gets - the more likely you will listen to it in game.
[*] Steam vote is the key vote, but we will hold other votes on Reddit (or other media) that will serve as a recommendation and hold less power. You can participate in both.
[*] You are encouraged to leave any feedback and/or suggest other tracks that could be added to the game. However, make sure you have stated your 5 choices clearly first.
[*] [b]The vote lasts from 21 July to 1 August.[/b] All later entries will not affect the results.[/list]

notes.title: Games Gathering 2021 Odessa
notes.notes:
Last week we travelled to another city in Ukraine - Odessa to our first offline game conference since the start of the pandemics.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/8047401830e7adb91a89c68e1a8360eedf190ca6.png[/img]

We have participated in the Indie Blast competition with the Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom and had a free demonstration space thanks to that. For 2 days anyone interested in our projects or cooperation with us could come to our desk and discuss any topics or just play the game and give us feedback. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/255a65724cbcc30937b4dd565d18f9770afdeff0.png[/img]

Our CEO and Founder Ihor Tymoshenko and Lead Game Designer / COO Oleksandr Sienin gave a joint talk about our company's path, financial results, and valuable lessons we have learned the hard way. The audience was very pleased and even surprised by the level of transparency and frankness we have shown throughout the talk, as few companies are ready to share all the sensitive information about them due to various reasons including NDAs. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/11675be974c6fa7d86c9c3abea968534bb0fe03e.png[/img]

Overall, we are very happy that we decided to spend these few days among like-minded people and had lots of interesting discussions. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/1602934435699ce59ab343d973ee1be2743c2127.png[/img]

There will be an even bigger from the same organizers in Kyiv - our hometown in December 2021, and we are looking forward to going there with everyone on the team who would want to participate. We plan to showcase Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty there. 

Hope you have enjoyed our short story.

Have a good day!

Due to a number of reasons we decided to extend the production time and plan the Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty release for Q1 2022, so it is not coming this winter holidays. notes.title: Developer’s Diaries #16
notes.notes:
Hello, guys! It is exactly one month after the Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom release and we want to share the first results with the community. As you may know we are always as transparent as possible about work and results.

[h1]The Strategic Mind games quality grows[/h1]

We monitor all of your feedback and we can see that although there is still huge room for improvement the overall feedback becomes more favourable with every title. Still, we better look at some tangible criteria for more precise and unbiased results.

[h2]Median time played[/h2]

Median does not mean average, it means that 50% of the players played longer than this number. Note that the average play times for later releases are likely to still grow:

[h3]Panzer Strategy[/h3]
Median time played: 2 hours 16 minutes.
Average time played: 23 hours 50 minutes.

[h3]Strategic Mind: The Pacific[/h3]
Median time played: 2 hours 23 minutes.
Average time played: 23 hours 58 minutes.

[h3]Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg[/h3]
Median time played: 4 hours 49 minutes.
Average time played: 49 hours 55 minutes.

[h3]Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism[/h3]
Median time played: 6 hours 6 minutes.
Average time played: 37 hours 53 minutes.

[h3]Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom[/h3]
Median time played: 8 hours 10 minutes - and keeps growing.
Average time played: 24 hours 44 minutes.

As you can see, there is a steady growth in the median time played which is a good indication that more players now enjoy the game for a longer period of time. 

[h2]Steam reviews [/h2]

We should, of course, account for the smaller sample size for the more recent projects. However, if we just look at the overall numbers we will see the following picture:

[h3]Panzer Strategy[/h3] 
417 reviews, 65% positive*.

[h3]Strategic Mind: The Pacific [/h3]
429 reviews, 76% positive*.

[h3]Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg[/h3]
271 reviews, 87% positive*.

[h3]Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism[/h3]
92 reviews, 92% positive*.

[h3]Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom[/h3]
37 reviews, 94% positive*.

*Only Steam purchasers’ reviews are counted. It would be even higher otherwise.

So, we can see that the Steam customers rate the games progressively better. 

[h1]The Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom - not so good release[/h1]

The most successful release so far was Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg. Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom got even better results in the first 12 hours - so we are grateful to our loyal community who supported us and got the game on release. 

However, this time we did not get nearly as much traffic from Steam. It is decided by very complex Steam algorithms that we do not know (to exclude any bias). Here is the number of visits from the two main sources of new visitors on Steam:

[h3]Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg 1 months after release[/h3]
Discovery queue visits: 136, 274.
Steam homepage visits: 124, 919.
[b]Total:[/b] 261, 193 visits.

[h3]Strategic Mind Fight for Freedom 1 months after release[/h3]
Discovery queue visits: 51, 033.
Steam homepage visits: 12, 605.
[b]Total:[/b] 63, 638 visits.

Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom got 4 times less exposure on Steam despite a more successful day 1 sales.

We did what we could to promote Fight for Freedom, and the community supported us on day 1. Afterwards, we got less exposure on Steam and consequently much lower overall sales. 

[h1]What the future holds[/h1]

Despite this unfortunate setback, we are already working hard on the Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty that might become the last Strategic Mind title. We will keep you updated on our production progress, but the first maps are already playable and go through the testing process. The Spirit of Liberty will most likely be released in Q1 2022. We will keep polishing all the Strategic Mind titles and keeping them up to date.

Support our efforts by adding Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty to your wishlist:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1474770/Strategic_Mind_Spirit_of_Liberty/

notes.title: Update 1.05
notes.notes:
Hello, guys!

Three weeks have passed since release and we have been hard at work fixing all sorts of issues reported by the players’ community. Now, we can say that we are 90% through, and we present most of the remaining fixes in today’s update. 

[h2][b]Update 1.05[/b][/h2]

[b]Bug fixes:[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed serious issue with the secondary objective in Battle of the Bulge. The enemy airforce damage counter was working incorrectly leading to a likely failure. Now that is fixed. It will work correctly from the save file, but the already counted value will remain. So, you might want to go back a couple of turns. (Reported by: mmtt)
[*] Fixed the Poor morale effect on the German air force (after completing the objective during Battle of the Bulge) to carry over to the USSR air force. If you already have this effect you have to finish any of the operations 5, 6, 7, 8, or 9 to get rid of it. (Reported by: Foxador)
[*] Fixed Searchlight Control "Elsie" in multiple ways. (Reported by: VirgoCompany and others)
 1) Now it cannot be installed together with other Radar and/or searchlights. 
 2) Now it does not provide a +2 Air attack regardless of the day/night time. 
 3) Its cost was lowered from 110 to 80 Prestige.
 4) Now it combines Radar and Heavy searchlight effect, but takes only 1 equipment slot (as was originally designed). So, It both reduces the Night attack penalty by 50% and adds a +3 Air attack ONLY at Night. 
[*] Added missing Victory hexes counter in the primary objective of Battle for Moscow. 
[/list]

[b]Description updates:[/b]
[list]
[*] Corrected Battle of the Bulge operation briefing to inform about the Winter operation. (Reported by: Foxador)
[*] Corrected Sniper squad equipment description.
[*] Corrected Small searchlight description. (Reported by: VirgoCompany)
[*] Corrected Medium searchlight description. (Reported by: VirgoCompany)
[*] Corrected Heavy searchlight description. (Reported by: VirgoCompany)
[*] Corrected Searchlight Control "Elsie" description.
[*] Corrected Radio combat support skill (Hero Audie Murphy) description. (Reported by: Foxador)
[*] Added Last stand effect description. 
[/list]

[b]Visual improvements[/b]
[list]
[*] Replaced V-1 models with V-2 models and correct launch pads in the secondary objectives hexes in operation Market Garden. 
[/list]

As you can see, most of the issues were reported by you guys, so your reports and feedback help us a lot. Right now, we have fixed most of the serious issues, but we will keep polishing and improving the game. Make sure you report any problems you face to our team on the community hub, or reach out to us by email: contact@starnigames.com

With best regards
Starni Games team

notes.title: Weekly Feature #7: HQ Skills
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=ig9aNobQJgI;full][/previewyoutube]
Hello guys! Today, we will explain the HQ skills mechanic in general and have a look at the list of HQ skills available in Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom. We hope this video will have you to better understand how this system works, as it provides an immense advantage on the battlefield. Please, let us know what you think of the system in general and about the particular HQ skills you prefer. 

[h2]About the Weekly feature series[/h2]
The Strategic Mind series has a quite sophisticated set of core mechanics, some of which are a novelty for the genre, for example, the supply system. The upside is that the game has lots to explore even for seasoned wargame veterans and offers everyone a new experience. The downside is that oftentimes the players lack the time to master all the core mechanics, especially after a hard working week, when you want to spend more time with your family during the weekend. 

We have decided to start a new series of short tutorial videos called Weekly feature. In this series, we will have a closer look at one core mechanic at a time. We hope that it will help the new players to grasp the game faster, and the veteran players to learn a couple of new tricks. For example, we will explain in more detail the Surrender mechanic or the damage calculation rules. It should be especially helpful to the players who are new to the wargame genre.

notes.title: Weekly Intelligence Report #31
notes.notes:
General! Our ever-vigilant intelligence service has prepared a news update, for your eyes only!
Here are all of our spy’s key findings.

[h2]SM: Fight for Freedom release. First results[/h2]

The Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom was released 10 days ago. While it is too early to judge, we can already see the first sales results, and they are quite discouraging. We will give you a more detailed report in the next Dev Diaries issue, but so far the release was underwhelming despite our best efforts to promote the game. It seems that this time we got much less traffic from Steam, despite decent day 1 sales compared to previous titles. The game was not featured in the “New and trending” tab (unlike all the previous titles). Technically it was, but only very briefly. So, we will gather all the data and explain all of it in Dev Diaries.

At the same time, we are happy that despite the low number of players - those of you who did find the game, left mostly positive feedback. So, we are happy that most players enjoy the game and find it of good quality. It is very important for us to know your opinion. There are not many reviews for now, which makes sense looking at the sales numbers, but most of them are positive, and we hope to keep that trend, by addressing all existing issues in a timely manner.

[h2]Issues with cinematics (already fixed)[/h2]

Many of you could have noticed that during the first week there were some issues with cinematics video and sound. The truth is that we could not finish and polish them properly before the planned release date, and we did not want to reschedule it, so we were trying to finish them in time for the release. Unfortunately, some of them were added last minute and there was literally no time to correct the sound for them. By next Friday we sorted out all these shortcomings. 

We are sorry for these issues, and will make sure to have better planning next time and have everything ready well in advance. There were some force majeure factors at play this time, like one of our 3D artists breaking right hand and being out of commission for about 2 months and other problems. We will tell you about it in more detail in Dev Diaries, so stay tuned. Nonetheless, we totally understand that the players should always receive the final and polished product, and no force majeure factors should affect that. That is why we will take a more measured approach next time, which will probably delay the release, but ensure that everything is in order. 

[h2]New Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom videos on YouTube[/h2]

We keep an eye on all new videos on YouTube that feature Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom. We can recommend these two channels as they seem to have done quite a good overview of the game. We will keep you informed of the new high-quality YouTube coverage of the game.

[h1]Update 1.03[/h1]

notes.title: 8 Days to Release - Douglas A-1 Skyraider The US Attack Aircraft
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/735bfbb3c9f0ef7335b2984bba27902e6dad1c28.png[/img]

In the age of the turbojet, Douglas A-1 Skyraider flew as a piston-powered, propeller-driven blast from the past. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/12bda2c534d744d6812578cee65c8d21ee4a0737.jpg[/img]

With the rapid development of jet aircraft towards the end of the war, dozens, if not hundreds of piston engine aircraft became obsolete. The Skyraider could have joined their lot, but its innovative turbo-compound engine gave it a chance to prove itself - and prove itself it did.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/500fbb2065c7709ed3a10144dbf984b50aac36e8.jpg[/img]

A solid, well-made and innovative at a time, Douglas A-1 would last well into the Vietnam War, only decommissioned in the 1970s. It was an attack aircraft that could shred ground targets with its 20-mm autocannons, carry out tactical bombings (with its payload capacity of 3600 kg) and deliver torpedo strikes equally well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/474ae69218b59df3733695829d035bdb30e3b894.jpg[/img]

There is no telling how effective Douglas A-1 would have been in WWII if it were finalized and deployed faster. And in Fight for Freedom, you’ll get to explore that exact possibility.

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/VwtOcFY2RCm98EZ3dN/giphy-downsized-large.gif[/img]

notes.title: Units in Fight for Freedom #19 | M45 - The US Assault Gun On a Tank Chassis
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/94e50495a494d2a271696615e5d2cf8afdcbe740.png[/img]

The expression “Texas-sized” exists for a reason. Throughout the 20th century, the Americans became known for their taste for massive, bombastic things, and the M45 definitely fit the description. Categorized as an assault gun, the idea was very simple: borrow a 105-mm howitzer from the Sherman’s assault variant and mount it on a heavy tank chassis, the precursor to the Pershing. Tough, low-profile and deadly, the M45 was designed for the European theatre, and was by far the most powerful assault gun to be fielded by the American Allies during WWII.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/e13da17c311e04868a2d7c46f662448046ab1085.jpg[/img]

And like many revolutionary projects, M45 arrived too late. It saw most of its service during the Korean war, where it had no unique niche to fill, and so quickly fell into obsolescence. However, in Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom, things can go very differently for M45.

[h2]M45 in SM: Fight for Freedom[/h2]

notes.title: Units in Fight for Freedom #18: American Jet Fighters - P-80 Shooting Star
notes.notes:
In mid-1943 when the Germans were already making impressive progress on their jet fighters. Still far from fully operational, the new machines showed great promise - and posed a massive threat: it was clear that whoever mastered the turbojet technology first would come to dominate the skies.

The U.S. War Department issued a call to action, and Lockheed’s Clarence Johnson answered. After countless hours of exhausting overtime, under strictest secrecy and dictatorial discipline, Johnson’s hand-picked crew created the prototype for P-80 “Shooting Star” - the first American jet fighter.

[h2]P-80A[/h2]
Slick futuristic silhouette, potential speed up to 600 mph/965 kph (living up to its nickname), and six .50-caliber machine guns - P-80A, the first mass-produced model, was both the beauty and the beast. Sadly, the jet was developed too late to see any frontline combat in WWII, but just in time for the wars to come.

[h2]P-80B[/h2]
The next variant, P-80B, had a better engine, thicker armor and could carry unguided missiles. It was the terror of the early stages of the Korean War. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/d90ec5471aaf562ae5d93be6dc6ae361658401cb.jpg[/img]

[h2]Shooting Star in Fight for Freedom[/h2]
All jet fighters in Strategic Mind - the German Me-262, the Soviet MiG-9, the British Gloster Meteor, and finally the US P-80A and P-80B are far superior to all previous non-jet models. So, they provide a very solid boost to your air force capabilities.

The Strategic Mind series has a quite sophisticated set of core mechanics, some of which are a novelty for the genre, for example, the supply system. notes.title: "The great Third Army and a son-of-a-goddamned-bitch named George Patton!" (c)
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/e48075521f80c223a5058bb922a1961202935746.png[/img]

Few generals have a record so varied and storied as George Patton did - fewer still have such a good time doing it. That isn’t to say he was a warmonger - more likely, he considered war simply the most prestigious and the most masculine of sports. And when it came to sports, it was Patton’s belief that 
“Americans love a winner and will not tolerate a loser. Americans play to win all the time.”

George Smith Patton Jr. was born in 1885 to a well-off family of a career soldier, and never considered being anything other than a military man. His record from West Point indicates as much — excellent performance in all things military. Including fencing, down to designing a new kind of cavalry sabre.

After Patton's first combat during the Mexican Revolution, he acquired a taste for it, and in WWI led a tank unit during the Meuse-Argonne Offensive. His steely resolve is encapsulated in the simple note he left in his diary on the eve of the battle: “Will start soon.”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/8ac062ca79a6874a6171154a90ddae2145494bb0.jpg[/img]

After the Great War, Patton became a large proponent of developing an armored warfare doctrine. He helped establish the US Armored Corps, taking cues from both the French and the Germans, and went down in history as one of the most successful armored commanders of all time. That isn’t to say serving with General Patton was easy on the best of days. He was a demanding disciplinarian, and a proponent of quick and aggressive action, nor did he pick his words very carefully. The grunts loved him for it, even if they knew he’d push them to the limit of their ability, but the HIgh Command considered him a time bomb. And several times, it did go off.

Patton often lacked subtlety, and he was by no means a unique case in the Allied Army. His frequent clashes with Montgomery, and their constant one-upmanship was a cause of many headaches in the High Command, and for Supreme Commander Eisenhower in particular. President Truman once wrote, 

“Don’t see how a country can produce such men as Robert E. Lee, John J. Pershing, Eisenhower and Bradley and at the same time produce Custers, Pattons and MacArthurs.”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/d7a6bf7a474c7259e63a0e8d243aa562830f2dc9.jpg[/img]

General Patton was also notorious for his dislike for Russians, describing them unfavorably after every single encounter with them. It was Patton’s belief that with Germany demilitarized and shared with the Soviets, and the US Army shrinking during peacetime, the Communist takeover of Europe was only a matter of time. 

“Now the horrors of peace, pacifism and unions will have unlimited sway,” he wrote. “I wish I were young enough to fight in the next [war].”

notes.title: Units in Fight for Freedom #17: Tortoise - a British Heavy Asault Tank/Gun
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/f97de65f4669dc3ed7c23cc45c7dba55c176cf67.jpg[/img]


Tortoise A39 was designed late into the war to combine extremely heavy armor planting with a gun powerful enough to wreck Panther at a 1 km range. It had both things British tanks were often lacking - armor and firepower. Yet, one cannot have it all. It lacked mobility and with a monstrous weight of 80 tons, it could only reach a maximum speed of 19 km/h on good roads. This shortcoming rendered it nearly useless for future operations and only 6 machines were built that proved otherwise fully functional and quite powerful. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/3cb8f433de7c581f67d93039c5fd20da0ddc6dd6.jpg[/img]

Tortoise did not see much action in WW2 and was considered far from ideal design. Still, its armor and firepower were more than formidable. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/4274be43444d996abe375b9321453bc683b20d5c.jpg[/img]
[h1]
Tortoise in Fight for Freedom[/h1]

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/5Tz9i3zWpqJ524icnq/giphy.gif[/img]

In the alternate history portion of the US campaign you will be able to acquire this powerful assault gun from your British allies and use it in your army to fight the Soviet renowned heavy tanks. Although not suitable for swift breakthroughs, it could help you gradually punch your way through the powerful Soviet units. having both high defense and attack it lacks in the Movement points department.

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/wP7q3S8CByX6sagSdO/giphy.gif[/img]

Would you still use Tortoise?

notes.title: Units in Fight for Freedom #16: US strategic bombers
notes.notes:
Carpet bombings make for some of the most striking images of the Second World War - there’s a reason why the sight of leveled cities was often described as “moonscape”. Not many planes were capable of bringing such destructive power across such great distances - and the United States Air Force had an entire series of them.

[h2]B-17[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/e07bbbf2ab5ab73fe9a767f2f19d6a0f08a85535.jpg[/img]

The legendary B-17 “Flying Fortress” was a sturdy and reliable machine. Its payload was respectable, and its overall performance sufficed for hundreds of bombing raids across the entire Germany. The largest raid ever conducted by the Americans on Berlin consisted mostly of B-17s - and their combined might was horrifying.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/f68c5d7f62b9d703b3ab379103b10fd2016c1279.jpg[/img]

[h2]B-29[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/eecc48cf2cc636514d5777838424bcc18e23be23.jpg[/img]

Then, B-29 came around, dubbed “Superfortress” - its payload was 9000 kg. They wrought havoc across the Pacific, including the firebombing of Tokyo, and the nuclear detonations over Hiroshima and Nagasaki - the three most destructive air raids in the history of mankind.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/8effe5dd14ab245fc9e96e07c494f66810243ec0.jpg[/img]

[h2]B-36[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/d0c3f0f8493caaa53969fd65ab20a9845d3026e5.jpg[/img]

B-36 was slated to become their successor, improved in every regard, but by 1946, it was too little, too late. Although, it is not too late for them in Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom, as we have an alternate history ending in 1946, allowing you to use B-36 in battle. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/edcb91a118cc1f68cd4d7f6ca977ba74151f1400.jpg[/img]

[h2]Strategic bombers in Fight for Freedom[/h2]

In the US campaign, for the first time in the Strategic Mind series, the player would have the 
option to acquire Strategic bombers as core units. All three units: B-17, B-29, and B-36 will be available for upgrades as one series, which makes upgrades cheaper. They will have passive ability Overwatch breakthrough (similar to that of the fighters, but no need to activate it). Another unique skill is Strategic bomber, that allows the flying fortresses to deal extra damage to infrastructure and reduce the ammo and fuel of the enemy units by destroying their supplies. On top of that their combat parameters, especially defense, will be quite high. All this glory comes at a hefty cost though, both for the acquisition and repair.

notes.title: Historical Personalities in Fight for Freedom #3: Field Marshal Harold Alexander
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/6b73cee24d727a544c23cc5b058c1306def7e5bb.png[/img]

Field Marshal, though General for most of WWII, Harold Alexander was no typical military man. Far from his generally gruff colleagues, Alexander had an artistic strea, being a lifelong painter, and was known for his likeable, if not necessarily agreeable personality. General Patton once said ”an army is a team” - Alexander fit the role of the fair and personable team captain. 

In France, North Africa, Burma and eventually Italy, Alexander led the Allied forces through personal charm, persuasion and mediation - an approach that sometimes bordered on manipulation. Some would say it was warranted, however, in an army full of talented but headstrong types.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/45a50fd462b2cd57cf0b457817245482b3289e89.png[/img]

Known for Alexander's impeccable manners and modesty, he had established good relations with the key decision makers, like Sir Winston Churchill and Supreme Allied Commander Dwight Eisenhower. The praise and the criticism usually centered on the same trait, simply observing it from a different angle. While some admired his laissez-faire approach, others faulted him for insufficient oversight; some admired Harold's honesty and modesty, others claimed it was a deliberately cultivated image. Some even framed his usual calm under pressure as complete detachment from combat. Field Marshals Montgomery and Brooke claimed he was “intellectually unimpressive”, though some suspect it was another display of modesty - after all, Alexander definitely had a keen mind for interpersonal relations.

The facts, however, spoke for themselves - Harold Alexander was an incredibly experienced war leader, who fought with equal efficiency in the mountains, deserts, jungles or plains. And in 1945, it was him who accepted the first major surrender of the German forces - a one million-strong group of armies in Italy.

notes.title: Units in Fight for Freedom #15: Centurion - the British main battle tank
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/8eb4e83d12b344a58d0648ac8d7cffd5b9109e22.png[/img]

The venerable Centurion embodied wartime research and development. It was built specifically to counter the then-strongest tank military on the planet, and was perfectly equipped for the task - only for the war to suddenly end. It stayed in service for decades, and spent years without a worthy foe.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/4eba0c1a8c54cb95cc23cc3c4c9bccfa46d68313.png[/img]

While being a heavy tank, with 150 mm turret armor, Centurion was conceived as the last of the Cruiser tanks. The goal was to maintain the series’ reliability, mobility and ease of maintenance, but improve its survivability and equip it with 17-pounder tank-killer cannons. The result was a resounding success - while less well-protected than the Churchill, it was the first truly “universal tank”, and paved the way for the MBTs of the Cold War and beyond.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/64c3bf4115598a65a3bdc8bc835875d89e980f33.jpg[/img]

Sadly, Centurion’s field trials came in April 1945, when the Victory in Europe was only a matter of time. Created to counter Panthers and Tigers, it ended up facing neither. However, in the alternative-history portion of Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom, things can play out very differently.

notes.title: Montgomery: Model Creation and Character Overview
notes.notes:
[h2]Field Marshal Bernard Law Montgomery[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/c2f60a206101e48e7e4e0f33bb777f7d372f14d0.png[/img]

It is a fact of life that sometimes, great things aren’t done by being nice about it. Sir Bernard Law Montgomery, 1st Viscount Montgomery of Alamein, had many mottos and creeds, but he seemed to downright exemplify this one.

Born to a minister’s family, Bernard Law Montgomery, was slated to become a clergyman, but opted instead for a soldiering life. It was, perhaps, for the best - while a man of many virtues, it’s hard to imagine humility among them. As his good friend Sir Winston Churchill put it: “In defeat, unbeatable. In victory, unbearable”.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/819dd2ea20cce81af43d68137c667a6112bffe80.jpg[/img]

Montgomery was known for his lack of social awareness and insensitivity: he was a self-assured leader, and bruised many egos in the Grand Alliance. But the soldiers loved Montgomery. With his gray sweater and tanker’s black beret, he had the image of a rebel, and chafed under unnecessary restrictions - at the same time, his asceticism and strict discipline earned him the moniker “the Spartan General”. Having been through the meatgrinder of the First World War, he took its lessons to heart, and cared about the troop morale, and preferred a systemic, low-risk strategy. When it came to beating the enemy, Montgomery liked to be “mathematically certain”, and waste no lives needlessly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/e85d7d66959882f209135e0e555f7a1e569837ee.jpg[/img]

His exploits were numerous, beginning with the battle of El Alamein, and the eventual defeat of General Rommel. But his finest hour came in 1944, when he was made Field Marshal and put in charge of the land troops in Operation Overlord, directing the Normandy landings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/ace491996a1b4177e168e86d3ebb45c24a7aba72.jpg[/img]

After the war, Field Marshal Montgomery played an instrumental role in the establishment and development of NATO. He served as the Deputy Supreme Allied Commander Europe until 1958, when he ended his illustrious military career and peacefully retired.

[h2]Montgomery’s character model creation[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/413b37bc32782b899cf2fe87b593a74e31c2ac80.jpg[/img]

We will also tell you a bit about the model creation process. Here is some footage from the editor, that allows you to see the character through the eyes of our 3D artists.
